Continuity of each compact mixed tail yields a finite attained rightmost Q quantile of mass Q, including if there is a plateau. At an exterior mark a strict separator from the canonical hull gives zero depth.

Positive depth gives own interior. A through-mark cap of mass Q has a proper own trace and locally strict tail there, so is a rightmost quantile. Conversely active quantile slack zero gives that mass and proper section. Strictly enclosing the mark at mass Q is excluded by a positive own-volume loss.
The positive scalar envelope derivative and the tangent inequality for concave E^(1/d) give both normal-cone implications; at zero parameter the minimizing first moment forces the own-fiber centroid.

Testing cone combinations against (h,−1) proves one implication. For the converse a separating (h,s) with a·h>0 gives a feasible positive multiple of h whether s is nonnegative or negative. The conic Carathéodory cardinality d+1 retains both small residual and nonnegative small total slack.

For any slot of positive limiting coefficient, bounded weight and vanishing slack force own threshold convergence to u·y. Finite-site compactification preserves that evaluation and exact mass Q; zero-weight slots have vanishing normal contribution. Conic Carathéodory in R^d gives at most d exact normals.

The Slater inequality bounds the weight, finite local inequalities give the polyhedral normal cone by small feasible steps, and positively spanning active normals force the singleton and span every optimizer vector conically.
